name: kobai
// scripts: Every command kobai has, in the file every other TypeScript repository keeps them in (ADR-0083). devbox.json declares none — it pins Node and enables corepack for whoever wants it, and `tests/devbox-declares-no-commands.test.ts` fails the build if a second list grows there. There is deliberately no `install` script: `pnpm install` is the command, and a script by that name is an npm lifecycle hook that would run during it. The `"// …"` keys below are inert — npm requires strict JSON, so a comment cannot go there, and npm attaches no meaning to such a key.

scripts.// ci: The gate. One command, and CI runs this one rather than a list of steps of its own — a step list is a second definition of green that can drift from this one, and `if it passes locally it passes here` is worth more than per-step timing. It installs nothing: you install, then you run the gate.
scripts.ci: pnpm run lint && pnpm run typecheck && pnpm run build && pnpm run test
scripts.// up: Postgres and the application. `build` then `up` rather than `up --build`, so the address prints between the build output and the log stream rather than scrolling away above a cold build. `scripts/serving-on.ts` prints it rather than the shell, because in a worktree the port lives in `.env` — which compose reads and the shell does not.
scripts.up: node scripts/ensure-env.ts && docker compose build && node scripts/serving-on.ts && docker compose up
scripts.// db: Just Postgres, which is what the test suite needs. `scripts/ensure-env.ts` gives a linked worktree a `.env` of its own first, so compose publishes that worktree's port and a hand-typed `docker compose up db` reaches the same container this does (ADR-0084).
scripts.db: node scripts/ensure-env.ts && docker compose up -d --wait db
scripts.// dev: The reference Project on this machine, against the Postgres in Docker. `scripts/dev.ts` exists to assemble one variable — DATABASE_URL, from the parts, at the moment it is needed. Nothing exports one, because a written-down URL goes stale the moment the password above it changes (#63).
scripts.dev: node scripts/ensure-env.ts && pnpm -r build && node scripts/dev.ts
scripts.// admin:dev: The Admin with a reload loop, in a second terminal beside `pnpm run dev`. A Vite dev server proxying /admin, /store and /health to the Project, so the browser still sees exactly one origin — which is what production looks like and why no CORS is configured anywhere (ADR-0010, ADR-0033).
scripts.test: node scripts/ensure-env.ts && docker compose up -d --wait db && pnpm run build && pnpm run browsers && vitest run
scripts.// browsers: The Chromium tests/the-admin-in-a-browser.test.ts drives. Playwright ships no browser in its npm package, so this is a download rather than an install. `--only-shell chromium` is the headless shell and not the whole browser, and it is asked for by name at launch — since Playwright 1.49 a bare `headless: true` launches the full browser in its new headless mode, which this deliberately does not download. `test` reaches this script rather than repeating it: a guardrail behind an opt-in step is not a faster guardrail, it is an optional one (ADR-0044).
scripts.// lint: `--error-on-warnings` because `biome ci` exits zero on warnings without it, and Biome 2 re-tiered most of what Biome 1 called an error down to `warn` or `info`. The flag covers the `warn` tier and every rule Biome adds to it later; biome.json lifts the `info` tier up to `warn`, which no flag can do. `ci` reaches this script rather than repeating its flags, so the two cannot drift — tests/the-lint-gate-fails-below-error.test.ts holds that. `format` is the forgiving one: it rewrites rather than reports.
scripts.// db:generate: Builds first because a Plugin's drizzle.config.ts imports defineKobaiDrizzleConfig from @kobai/core/migrations, and that specifier resolves through the package's `exports` to dist — the same path a Plugin author outside this repository takes. Recursive because every package that owns tables generates its own migrations from its own schema, Core included.
scripts.// db:push: There is deliberately no db:push script, and this is now the file where someone would reach for the convenient one. `drizzle-kit push` diffs against the LIVE database: run against a database holding Plugin tables it reports success and silently DROPS them, leaving their migration tracking rows behind so the migration runner believes the work is done and cannot repair it. Generate a migration instead. Observed, not theorised — FINDINGS.md section E on branch prototype/drizzle-multi-migration, and docs/adr/0030-generate-and-migrate-only-never-drizzle-kit-push.md. tests/no-push-script.test.ts fails the build if one appears here, in any package manifest, or in a CI workflow.
scripts.// openapi:generate: Needs neither a build nor a database: Node runs the TypeScript directly, and the description is a property of the routes rather than of anything behind them. The order is not incidental — pnpm walks the workspace in dependency order, so @kobai/core writes openapi.json and @kobai/client then regenerates itself from what Core wrote.
scripts.// template:generate: Rewrites what `create-kobai` generates from the reference Project, which is the source of truth for both. Run it after changing anything under `reference/`; tests/create-kobai-matches-the-reference-project.test.ts regenerates the template and compares it byte for byte, so the gate stays red until you do.

// pnpm.overrides: Overrides, and only ever for a security advisory Dependabot cannot fix by itself — see AGENTS.md § Dependency updates. Each entry is SCOPED to the one parent that pulls the vulnerable copy, so it moves that copy forward and nothing else, and a future advisory in the same package still surfaces as its own alert. An override is a forward bump; never write one that pins a package backwards. Delete an entry the moment its parent ships a release that no longer needs it, and check that first — an override outliving its reason is a pin nobody chose.
// pnpm.overrides.openapi-typescript>und: openapi-typescript@6.7.6 is the last 6.x and depends on `undici: ^5.28.4`, so no 6.x release exists for Dependabot to bump to and the whole undici 5 advisory backlog (#69: twelve alerts, three of them high) could never close on its own. 6 is pinned exactly because 7 needs a TypeScript compiler API that TypeScript 7 does not ship — see AGENTS.md § 'There is no TypeScript compiler API' — so the parent cannot move either. ^7.29.0 is above the first patched version of every one of the twelve advisories, and it is the copy @dotenvx/dotenvx and shadcn already resolve to, so this removes undici 5 from the tree rather than adding a third copy. Safe on three counts, one for each place openapi-typescript touches undici. dist/utils.js and its CJS twin dist/index.cjs reach for one value, `fetch`, and only as a fallback when `globalThis.fetch` is undefined — which under the Node 22 of ADR-0031 it never is, so undici issues no request of any kind and none of the twelve advisories (WebSocket, cookie, CRLF, keep-alive alike) has a path to run. `packages/client/generate.ts` never gives the generator a URL anyway; it hands it a parsed object read off disk. dist/types.d.ts imports three TYPES — RequestInfo, RequestInit, Response — and undici 7 still declares all three, which `pnpm run ci` proves by typechecking @kobai/client against it rather than by anyone's reading.
// pnpm.overrides.@esbuild-kit/core-util: drizzle-kit@0.31.10 — still the latest 0.31.x, and 1.0 is beta/rc only, so #28's and #9's 'unfixable, already latest' still holds — declares the deprecated @esbuild-kit/esm-loader, which pins `esbuild: ~0.18.20` and so carried GHSA-67mh-4wv8-2f99. drizzle-kit imports it nowhere (it only appears in that package's own manifest; the code uses its own esbuild ^0.25.4 and tsx), so this bump deduplicates onto the 0.25.x copy drizzle-kit already resolves rather than installing anything new. ^0.25.0 is the advisory's first patched version.
// devDependencies: The guardrail suite under `tests/` and nothing else — every package's own toolchain is that package's. Two of these are the browser seam's (#175, ADR-0063): `playwright` drives a real Chromium against a really-booted reference Project, and `axe-core` is evaluated into the page it is looking at. Both are here rather than in `reference/admin/` because the test that uses them is here; the Admin's bundle contains neither, which `tests/admin-uses-only-the-public-api.test.ts` still holds. The npm package ships no browser — `pnpm run browsers` downloads one, and `pnpm run ci` runs that itself.
